summary: Maryland-Delaware line tower (1931, jointly owned, rebuilt 1938 to 130 ft overall); listed standing, last condition record a 2007 Maryland DNR report (fair).

facts.design: Steel tower with an inside wooden stairway to a 7 ft square cab, upper half glass; rebuilt in 1938 on a 20 ft bottom extension
facts.status_note: Listed as standing by Forest Fire Lookout Association lists. Last condition record found is a Maryland DNR report from April 2007 (fair). Current condition not verified.
facts.agency: Maryland and Delaware forestry departments, jointly owned; the 2007 Maryland DNR report lists the Forest Service as managing agency

events.note: Erected with the other Eastern Shore towers, work from 29 July to 15 October 1931; jointly owned and operated by Delaware and Maryland. Report gives 100 ft to cab floor, 110 ft overall.
Denton Journal (28 October 1933) announced Emory Williamson as the new towerman, to be placed on duty when weather allows. The 1939 account spells the name Emery.
Joint Maryland-Delaware agreement to reconstruct and heighten the Interstate tower with new piers and a 20 ft bottom extension (FY 1937 State Forester report).
Dismantled and reconstructed on a 20 ft bottom extension during the winter; 120 ft to cab floor, 130 ft overall. Maryland supplied materials, Delaware labor through CCC.
Emery Williamson named again as towerman, under a two-year alternating funding arrangement.
Maryland DNR fire tower report (April 2007): forestry tower present, 120 ft, condition fair; deed carries a reversion clause.

corrections.why: 6.1 m (20 ft) matches no source read. The 1931 report gives 100 ft to the cab floor (110 ft overall). The 1938 rebuild made it 120 ft to the cab floor and 130 ft overall, which is the figure used here.

corrections.proposed: Maryland and Delaware forestry departments (jointly owned); the 2007 DNR report lists the Forest Service as managing agency
corrections.why: The current value is a location string, not an agency. The 1931 report says the two states jointly owned and operated the tower.

resolved_conflicts.explanation: The 1931 report says the tower lies along the Bridgeville-Denton highway; the 2007 DNR report places it on Route 404 at the state line. Both put it at the Maryland-Delaware line, so both are kept.

notes_for_editor: Brief record was wrong on height (6.1 m; the tower is 130 ft overall since 1938) and on the agency field, which holds a location string. Standing status comes from Forest Fire Lookout Association lists; the last condition record found is the April 2007 Maryland DNR report (fair). No later condition or access rules found, so no access key is given. The brief's coordinates (38.80156, -75.72056) match the Maryland list; the Delaware list gives 38.79917, -75.72111. A WebSearch snippet claimed a 2007 Delaware inventory marked the tower standing and called it the only one left; that page was not fetched, so it is not used. The Cape Gazette feature returned HTTP 403 and was not used. Used 1 WebSearch and about 5 page reads.
